advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drain git archive's stderr before/concurrently with archive.wait() (e.g. read stderr then wait, or use communicate) to avoid a stderr pipe-buffer deadlock.
evidence: tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py:103: `archive.wait()`
tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py:104: `failure = (archive.stderr.read() if archive.stderr else b"").decode("utf-8", "replace")`
stderr= subprocess.PIPE is set at line 84 but is only drained after wait(); a full stderr pipe buffer during a large/failed archive deadlocks the process
advisory.finding: extract_store_snapshot calls archive.wait() before reading archive.stderr, which can deadlock: git archive writes to both stdout (drained by tar) and a captured stderr PIPE; if git emits more than the OS pipe-buffer (~64KB) to stderr before exiting, it blocks on the stderr write while wait() blocks on the process exiting, and stderr is only read after wait() returns.
advisory.suggested_fix: Read `archive.stderr` (the buffer is closed at exit) before calling `archive.wait()`, or capture git's stderr to a temp file rather than a PIPE.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make reclaim() surface a failed rmtree (or verify the path is gone) rather than swallowing all errors with ignore_errors=True.
evidence: tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py:125: `shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)`
tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py:120: docstring: `Delete a finished store copy so concurrent modules do not sum their peaks.`
test_reclaim_removes_a_finished_copy asserts removal only for a fresh removable tree; a live reclaim that silently fails to free space produces no signal
advisory.finding: reclaim() uses shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True), so a failure to delete the finished store copy is completely silent — the check that the disk is reclaimed cannot distinguish 'reclaimed successfully' from 'reclaim never freed anything'. This is the exact failure the ticket exists to prevent (runner disk exhaustion), and on the live lane it would silently recur.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use shutil.rmtree(work) with an onerror handler that logs/raises, or after ignore_errors=True assert `not work.exists()` so a failed reclaim is not silent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the AST/text grep of _dc_fixtures.py in test_the_snapshot_is_not_buffered_whole_in_memory with a behavioral memory/streaming assertion (or drop it in favor of a peak-RSS/pipe observation).
evidence: tree = ast.parse(_FIXTURES.read_text())
assert not archives, "git archive is invoked as a list of argv parts, not a shell string"
assert "subprocess.Popen" in _FIXTURES.read_text(), "the streaming pipe is gone"
Docstring: 'Read structurally so the guarantee cannot regress by someone reinstating a capture elsewhere in the module.'

ABSENCE: no assertion drives extract_store_snapshot and observes bounded memory; a behavior-preserving rewrite (os.pipe, a helper, building argv differently) breaks the test while streaming behavior is unchanged
advisory.finding: test_the_snapshot_is_not_buffered_whole_in_memory asserts on the AST structure and literal text of the source under test (_dc_fixtures.py) — that 'git archive' is not a string constant, that no subprocess call passes input= with a ['tar', ...] list, and that the substring 'subprocess.Popen' is present — rather than exercising the function's observable memory/streaming behavior. This is source-grepping of executable source code and a change-detector.
scenarios: A future refactor streams via os.pipe or a factory helper instead of subprocess.Popen, keeping constant memory, but the test fails on the literal 'subprocess.Popen' check

advisory.finding: test_the_local_ticket_entry_rule_matches_the_harnesss_own compares the unparsed AST return-expression text of two source functions (_dc_support.is_ticket_entry vs _dc_fixtures._is_ticket_entry) instead of comparing their observable outputs over inputs. It breaks on a behavior-preserving rewrite of either predicate.
merged_from: test_every_store_copy_fixture_reclaims_its_tree greps the fixture source files for the literal substrings 'reclaim(work)' and 'yield work' as its pass/fail signal, instead of verifying that the fixtures actually reclaim their store copy on teardown. This is source-grepping of source under test and a change-detector.
scenarios: _is_ticket_entry is rewritten to `return name[:1] != '.'` (same behavior); the AST text comparison fails despite identical observable results
advisory.suggested_fix: Iterate a fixed list of names (dotfiles, canonical ids, bridge names, empty) and assert _dc_support.is_ticket_entry(n) == _dc_fixtures._is_ticket_entry(n) for each.
